guarantees.claim: When prng_reseed_rate equals PER_1, ctrl_wd.prng_reseed_rate is driven to PER_1.
When prng_reseed_rate equals PER_64, ctrl_wd.prng_reseed_rate is driven to PER_64.
When prng_reseed_rate equals PER_8K, ctrl_wd.prng_reseed_rate is driven to PER_8K.
For any other value of prng_reseed_rate, ctrl_wd.prng_reseed_rate is driven to PER_1.

assumptions.claim: The input prng_reseed_rate is expected to take only the three enumerated values PER_1, PER_64, PER_8K during normal operation.
assumptions.risk: An unsupported value would silently change the PRNG reseed interval to PER_1, potentially weakening security or causing unintended side-channel behavior.

uncertain_points.claim: Unsupported values are mapped to PER_1 by default, but it is unclear whether PER_1 is the safest fallback (could maximize reseed frequency but might also increase side-channel leakage or entropy exhaustion).
uncertain_points.risk: If PER_1 is not the intended safe reseed rate, a fault or attack could impose a weak reseed interval, degrading cryptographic randomness properties.

uncertain_points.claim: Unsupported prng_reseed_rate values are silently mapped to PER_1 without any alert or error indication, potentially masking configuration faults or attacks.
uncertain_points.risk: A fault that flips the reseed rate configuration may go undetected, degrading the PRNG’s security properties with no warning.

uncertain_points.claim: The set of legal encodings for prng_reseed_rate (defined in another module) may include more than PER_1, PER_64, PER_8K; need to verify that all defined values are intentionally handled and that the default mapping is correct for any unused encodings.
uncertain_points.cond: when the encoding definition is examined
uncertain_points.risk: A missing case item would incorrectly map a legal encoding to PER_1, causing a mismatch with the specification.
